info.aboutText: Keen Eye is a spot-the-difference game with living scenes. No ads, no internet.
info.privacyText: We collect no data at all. Progress and settings are stored only on your device.

timeMode.rules: The same place in the morning and in the evening, in summer and in winter. Light, snow and leaves change on their own — find what shouldn't have changed.

traps.moon: It's just the moon — that's how evenings are
traps.stars: Stars come out in the evening — not a difference
traps.lights: Lights go on in the evening — that's how it should be
traps.shadow: Shadows change with the sun — not a difference
traps.birds: The birds have flown away — that's natural
traps.snow: Everything is snowy in winter — that's how it should be
traps.leaves: Trees lose their leaves in winter — not a difference
traps.ice: Water freezes in winter — that's how it should be
traps.snowman: Someone made a snowman — not a difference
traps.clothes: People dress warmly in winter — that's natural
traps.icicles: Icicles only grow in winter — not a difference
traps.smoke: The stove is lit in winter — the smoke is natural
traps.flowers: Flowers and mushrooms don't grow in winter — that's natural
traps.clock: Time goes by — the clock should show a different time

memoryMode.rules: Remember the picture — you only get a few seconds. Then it changes: find what is different from memory. Up to 3 misses.
memoryMode.legend: Red circles show what you missed

worldTravel.rules: Travel the world: spot the differences in each place, learn an interesting fact about it and get a stamp in your passport.

facts.paris: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. It was meant to be taken down after 20 years, but it stayed and became the symbol of Paris.
facts.venice: Venice is spread over more than a hundred small islands: it has canals instead of streets, and boats and gondolas instead of cars.
facts.amsterdam: Many old houses in Amsterdam stand on wooden piles driven deep into the soft, marshy ground.
facts.tokyo: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan. On a clear day you can see it right from Tokyo.
facts.agra: The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife. Its walls are covered in white marble.
facts.greatWall: The Great Wall of China was built and extended over many centuries. It is not one wall but a whole chain of walls and towers across mountains and plains.
facts.yerevan: Yerevan is called the “pink city”: many of its buildings are made of pink volcanic stone called tuff. On a clear day you can see Mount Ararat from here.
facts.baku: Baku lies on the shore of the Caspian Sea, the largest lake on Earth. The city is below sea level, which makes it the lowest-lying capital in the world.
facts.tbilisi: The name Tbilisi comes from the Georgian word “tbili”, meaning “warm”: hot sulphur springs flow out of the ground here.
facts.newYork: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to America. It crossed the ocean in pieces and was unveiled in 1886.
facts.rio: The statue of Christ the Redeemer stands with open arms on top of Corcovado mountain, high above Rio de Janeiro.
facts.giza: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World that still stands today.
facts.safari: A giraffe's neck is very long, yet it has as many vertebrae as a human neck: just seven.
facts.sydney: The roofs of the Sydney Opera House look like sails filled with wind. The theatre opened in 1973.
facts.southernAlps: The kiwi is a bird that cannot fly. It is the symbol of New Zealand, and New Zealanders are often called “Kiwis” too.
facts.london: Big Ben is not the tower but the great bell inside it. The clock tower itself is called the Elizabeth Tower.
facts.barcelona: Work on the Sagrada Família began in 1882, and the architect Antoni Gaudí devoted more than 40 years of his life to it.
facts.athens: The Parthenon on the Acropolis was built almost 2,500 years ago for the goddess Athena — and, as the legend goes, the city is named after her too.
facts.prague: Prague’s astronomical clock, the Orloj, was installed in 1410. It is one of the oldest working astronomical clocks in the world.
facts.istanbul: Istanbul lies on two continents at once, Europe and Asia. The Bosphorus strait runs between them.
facts.dubai: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world: it is 828 metres high.
facts.bangkok: Thai people call their capital Krung Thep, “City of Angels”. And Bangkok’s full name is one of the longest city names in the world.
facts.singapore: The symbol of Singapore is the Merlion, half lion and half fish. The name Singapore itself means “lion city”.
facts.seoul: On Seoul’s main square stands a statue of King Sejong, who created the Korean alphabet, Hangul, in the 15th century.
facts.marrakesh: Marrakesh is called the “Red City”: its old walls and houses are built of reddish clay.
facts.capeTown: The top of Table Mountain is flat like a table. When clouds cover it, people say the mountain has laid its “tablecloth”.
facts.toronto: For more than 30 years the CN Tower was the tallest free-standing structure in the world. It has a glass floor you can walk on high above the city.
facts.mexicoCity: Mexico City stands where the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan once was — a city built on an island in the middle of a lake.
facts.cusco: Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire. The Incas fitted the stones of their walls so tightly that not even a knife blade fits between them.
facts.buenosAires: Buenos Aires is known as the birthplace of tango, and the bright houses of La Boca were once painted with leftover ship paint.
facts.moscow: St. Basil’s Cathedral on Red Square was built in the 16th century, and each of its domes is decorated differently.
facts.astana: The Bayterek tower shows a fairy-tale tree of life holding the golden egg of the magic bird Samruk at its top. Inside the golden sphere there is an observation deck.
